Plan, leg by leg:
- `tests/state-exams/exam-page.test.ts` — leg (a) [M1] over a plain `globalThis.window` (the shape of `client/test/todos-store.test.ts` leg (e)): flag true -> `readExamFlag()` true and `createTodosStore()` is `toBe` `window.__TINYAPP_STORE__`; `{}` -> false and the handle undefined; window deleted -> false, no throw; `{}` + seed -> handle's `getContent()` deep-equals the two-open-todos content. The module is imported as a namespace (`import * as sd`) so that at BASE the missing `readExamFlag` fails its own leg rather than failing the whole file to link, leaving legs (d) and (e) readable. Leg (d) [M4] is the one `stateExam({…})`, spelled exactly as the Proof gives it. Leg (e) [M5] asserts the two `sed | grep` patterns over AGENTS.md's Key Files section and spawns the `bun test` over the two BASE render exams, expecting exit 0.
- `client/test/exam-page.test.ts` — legs (b) and (c) [M2, M3] in the shape of `client/test/seeded-store-global.test.ts`: register a window only if none is registered, `mock.module` `../src/sqlite` (one sentinel `db` object), both TinyBase link factories and `reconnecting-websocket` before the dynamic imports, count sockets/getDb/synchronizers in module-level counters, render `Provider` + `Store` + a `useStore(STORE_ID)` probe, settle 300 ms, blank `globalThis.happyDOM` before `unregister()` in `afterAll`. Approach for task 1 (exam flag):

- `client/src/storeData.ts`: add `readExamFlag(): boolean` mirroring `readSeed` (no parameter, `read` prefix, so the linter's callback list in `lint-cli.test.ts` is untouched); `createTodosStore` exposes the store when seeded OR when the flag is up.
- `client/src/Store.tsx`: read the flag once at mount beside the seed; set `window.__TINYAPP_DB__` in the persister factory right after `await getDb()` and `window.__TINYAPP_PERSISTER__` in the `then` callback right after `await persister.load()` resolves, both only under the flag. Hooks stay unconditional: `useCreateSynchronizer` moves into a `SyncLink` child that `StoreLinks` mounts only when the flag is down.
- Handles are cleared at `Store` mount so a second render in one process (or a page that once held a seed) never reads the previous render's `__TINYAPP_DB__`/`__TINYAPP_PERSISTER__` — the same rule `exposeStore` already applies to `__TINYAPP_STORE__`.
- `client/src/vite-env.d.ts`: `__TINYAPP_EXAM__?: boolean` beside `__TINYAPP_SEED__` (the two globals a harness sets *into* the page); `__TINYAPP_DB__`/`__TINYAPP_PERSISTER__` beside `__TINYAPP_STORE__` in storeData's `declare global` (the three the page hands *out*).
- `client/src/sqlite.tsx` is left alone: M2 mocks `getDb`, so the assignment has to live in the persister factory to be observable.
- `AGENTS.md`: one bullet under `## Key Files` after the seeded-page bullet, naming EXAM, DB, PERSISTER in that order.

payload.body:
Approach for task 2 (the persistence move).

Plan, in the order the Context spells the move:
- `types.ts`: add `PersistenceExamSpec`; `ExamRecord` gains optional `rows` and `domBefore`, `walls` gains optional `persist_ms`/`reload_ms` (all optional so every BASE record still typechecks).
- `render-move.ts`: `renderHtml`'s `parts.seed` becomes optional; the seed `<script>` is skipped when absent. Nothing else in that function moves, so the seeded output stays byte-identical.
- `browser.ts`: `connect` gains a persistent listener registry beside its one-shot `once`; `Page` gains an optional `reload()` (arms `Page.loadEventFired`, sends `Page.reload`, awaits it — so the readiness poll after a reload can never read the outgoing document's globals); `Browser` gains an optional `openUrl({url, origin, clock, prelude})` that enables `Fetch` over `*` and answers every `requestPaused` with `continueRequest` for `<origin>/…` and `failRequest BlockedByClient` for everything else. Both new members optional, so the stand-ins in `state-exam.test.ts` and `browser-exam.test.ts` stay assignable.
- `persistence-move.ts`: `contentOf` (hand-written strip of the stamped `[[tables,hlc,hash],[values,hlc,hash]]` shape, dropping `\uFFFC`/`null` cells and the rows and tables they empty), `READY_TIMEOUT_MS`/`PERSIST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `runPersistenceExam` and `persistenceExam`.
- fixture under `test/fixtures/persistence/`, `capture-plugin.ts`'s `EXAM_NO_OPS`, README paragraph.

Two decisions worth writing down now:
1. The breach is read inside the readiness poll, not after it. A page that constructs a `WebSocket` at load throws out of its module and therefore never sets `__TINYAPP_PERSISTER__`; checking the breach only after readiness would report M7's ready timeout instead of M4's exact `contract breach: …`.
2. `app.js` puts everything after the `/` → `/room` redirect inside the `else` branch. At top level the `/` document would keep running and could set `__TINYAPP_PERSISTER__` before the redirect commits, and the exam would then call the pre-redirect document ready.

Two files, as the Proof names them.

`packages/tinyapp-exam/test/persistence-move.test.ts` carries legs (a)-(g) and (i). It imports the package as a namespace (`import * as exam from 'tinyapp-exam'`) rather than by name, so that at BASE each leg is red on its own missing helper (`tinyapp-exam exports no \`runPersistenceExam\` yet`) instead of the whole file failing to link; leg (a) reads the three new names and the twenty-four BASE names off that namespace, which is what M1 asks for. The browser legs skip with one printed line when neither $TINYAPP_BROWSER nor /headless-shell/headless-shell is on the machine, as browser.test.ts does.

`tests/state-exams/persistence-exam.test.ts` carries leg (h): the one top-level `persistenceExam({…})` over M5's spec, the one top-level `stateExam({…})` of the seeded regression, the red registration spawned as a child `bun test`, and the name pin. That file imports the three names *by name* — M1 wants exactly that, and at BASE its link failure is the absent implementation.

The variant pages are built inside each test body from the fixture's own `app.js`: the never-ready one renames `__TINYAPP_PERSISTER__`, the never-persisting and rows-gone ones append an `exec` override (the rows-gone one keyed on `document.body.dataset.load === '2'`, which M5 pins), the breach one appends the `new WebSocket('ws://localhost:8787/')`, and the leak one prepends an accessor for `__TINYAPP_PERSISTER__` that runs the cross-origin fetch first and only then hands the handle over — so `data-other` is settled before the driver calls the page ready, which is what leg (c) needs to read it off `record.dom`. Every wall is asserted finite and non-negative only, never bounded.

examiner (round 1): both exam files are written and the pair is red at BASE for the absent implementation only.

At BASE, `bun test tests/state-exams/exam-page.test.ts client/test/exam-page.test.ts` is 6 pass / 6 fail in ~5 s. The six red:
- leg (a) x3 — `storeData.readExamFlag` is undefined (the fourth leg-(a) test, the seeded `createTodosStore(seed)` half, is green at BASE by design: M1 says 'as at BASE, flag or no flag');
- leg (b) x2 — the flagged unseeded render leaves `__TINYAPP_STORE__`/`__TINYAPP_DB__`/`__TINYAPP_PERSISTER__` unset;
- leg (e) — the first `sed | grep` over AGENTS.md, the bullet not being there yet.
Green at BASE and meant to stay green: leg (c) both renders (M3's 'BASE's behaviour'), leg (d)'s `stateExam`, and leg (e)'s second grep and its nested `bun test` over the two BASE render exams.

Checked the other way too: a throwaway reference implementation (`readExamFlag` in `storeData.ts`, `exposeStore` widened by the flag, `__TINYAPP_DB__` set in `Store.tsx`'s persister factory after `await getDb()`, `__TINYAPP_PERSISTER__` in the `then` after `await persister.load()`, the synchronizer moved into a `SyncLink` child mounted only when the flag is false, and the AGENTS.md bullet) turns the pair 12 pass / 0 fail and leaves `bun run --cwd client tsc --noEmit` clean. That scratch implementation was reverted; the tree carries only the two test files.

Two readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. **Where `window.__TINYAPP_DB__` must be assigned.** M2 mocks `getDb` of `client/src/sqlite` to resolve `{sqlite3: {}, db: <one sentinel object>}` and still asks for `window.__TINYAPP_DB__` to be that sentinel. With the module replaced wholesale, an assignment made *inside* `getDb` cannot run — so M2 decides between the Context's two permitted placements: the assignment has to be in the persister factory in `client/src/Store.tsx`, right after `await getDb()`. The exam encodes M2; the note is in the file's header comment too.

2. **Why `storeData` is imported as a namespace in the state-exam file.** A named import of `readExamFlag` fails the whole module to link at BASE, which would take legs (d) and (e) down with it and make the red read as a bad import. As `storeData as unknown as {readExamFlag?: () => boolean}`, the absent export is leg (a)'s own first assertion (`typeof ... === 'function'`) and nothing else moves.

One environment fact worth recording, because it cost a 120 s timeout to find: `bun test` with both Proof paths on the command line does **not** run them in the order given — it runs `client/test/exam-page.test.ts` first — so the client file's globals are in place while the state exam's browser move runs. The client file therefore captures the `WebSocket` descriptor *before* `GlobalRegistrator.register()` and restores it in `afterAll`; captured after registration it restores happy-dom's window-bound constructor over Bun's native one, and `browser.ts`'s `new WebSocket(url)` CDP connect then hangs until the exam's 120 s wall. Nothing about the implementation — but any rewrite of that file has to keep the capture above the `register()` call.

Mechanism, measured under Bun 1.4.0 on this image: `Bun.build` honours a tsconfig `paths` map when it runs under `bun run`/`bun -e` (it walks to the nearest tsconfig of the entrypoint and finds `client/tsconfig.json`), but under `bun test` it looks only at the repository-root tsconfig — and 7d578da added `@/*` imports to `client/src/*` without adding a root tsconfig. Minimal repro: a one-test file whose body is `Bun.build({entrypoints: ["client/src/index.tsx"], plugins: [tailwind]})` fails under `bun test` and succeeds under `bun -e`. The Context for this task records its measurements under Bun 1.4.2, so this is plausibly a version difference rather than something anyone saw when 7d578da landed.

Fix taken, out of FILES and declared as an amendment: a new root `tsconfig.json` carrying only `{"compilerOptions": {"paths": {"@/*": ["./client/src/*"]}}}`. Additive — no project references it, `bun run typecheck` drives each package with an explicit `-p`/`--cwd`, and `client/tsconfig.json`'s own `paths` still governs the client build. With it: that Run line is 45 pass / 0 fail, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint:state` and `bun run lint:ui` all exit 0.

If a sibling task lands its own root tsconfig, keep whichever has the `@/*` map; two are a conflict, none is this red again.

Measured both ways over the full suite: with the root tsconfig 534 pass / 5 fail, without it 537 pass / 2 fail. It trades nine reds for five different ones, so it is not a fix. Reverted; `git status` is clean of it.

The measured BASE-vs-tree comparison, so nobody re-derives it:
- full `bun test`: BASE 537 pass / 2 fail, task-2 tree 537 pass / 2 fail — the same two, both `[M6]` meta-legs that spawn a child `bun test`.
- `bun test packages/tinyapp-lint packages/tinyapp-exam`: BASE 100 pass / 29 fail, task-2 tree 100 pass / 29 fail — identical test for test.
- the Proof's fifth `Run:` line, `bun test packages/tinyapp-exam/test/{state-exam,evidence,render-move}.test.ts`: BASE 36 pass / 9 fail, task-2 tree 36 pass / 9 fail.

So task 2 introduces no regression, and that fifth `Run:` line is red at BASE for a reason task 2 neither caused nor can reach. All 29 have one cause: under Bun 1.4.0 in this sandbox, `Bun.build` inside a `bun test` process resolves tsconfig `paths` from the repository-root tsconfig only, and 7d578da added `@/*` imports to `client/src/*` with no root tsconfig to map them — so every leg that goes through `bundleOf` or `ctx.render` on the client entry dies as `Could not resolve: "@/components/ui/button"`. The same build under `bun run`/`bun -e` succeeds, because there it walks to `client/tsconfig.json`. The Context for task 2 records its measurements under Bun 1.4.2, so this is likely a version difference.

A real fix belongs to whoever owns `client/` or the toolchain pin, and has to be one of: rewrite the `@/…` imports to relative paths; or pin Bun to 1.4.2 on the image; or give the root a tsconfig AND move the five tests that shell out to `tsc` onto `--ignoreConfig`. None of those is in task 2's FILES.

Everything task 2 does own is green: `bunx tsc -p packages/tinyapp-exam --noEmit`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint:state` (0 findings over 20 snapshots and 24 exams), `bun run lint:ui`, the `grep` and the README `sed | grep`.
